16" meat-lovers: 350 per slice (12 servings), or 4200 per pizza

Ever wanted to know the nutritional information of a Costco pizza?

You know, now that you mention it, it was interesting!

Really? Just because it's "pizza" doesn't mean I've abandoned sanity for the day. That's the whole reason I tried to find the nutritional information. Now I know the impact of my decision to eat a slice of pizza. So, my "slice" is essentially 2 servings, which I now know to be roughly 700 calories. Add to that my salad and I'm at 1000 cal for dinner. I eat a pretty consistent 400 for breakfast and lunch is typically 600-800. All told, I'm below my 2200 maximum intake and I haven't committed any nutritional hate crimes. Is pizza the best food choice to make? No. Can you make far worse choices? Yes. Is it possible to rationally make that call without knowing the nutritional information of something? Not really.
I think it's a safe assumption amongst most people that pizza is a poor dietary choice, regardless of the specifics.
How is regular cheese pizza the most calorie dense? Does this mean I should pile bacon, ham and sausage on top of other things to make them healthier?

It's because Costco, for whatever reason, really piles on the cheese (3 types) for this one. Think of it this way, each of their pizzas weighs the same, and the weight component of sauce and crust is identical for all of them ([W]eight = [C]rust + [S]auce + [T]oppings). So, in the case of cheese pizza versus meatlovers, you are comparing T of cheese to T of meat. Cheese is more calorically dense than meat, so there are more calories. This is also why the pepperoni is less than a meatlovers, which contains sausage.
